proposals.before: On guimao in the third month of Huangchu 4 under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), the moon occulted Antares, the bright star of the Heart mansion.
proposals.after: On guimao in the third month of Huangchu 4 under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), the moon transgressed Antares, the bright star of the Heart mansion.
proposals.reason: Chinese 犯 means transgression or approach, not a demonstrated occultation; the literal field already uses transgressed.

proposals.before: That November Prince Jian of Dongwuyang passed away.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, passed away.
proposals.reason: 十一月 is a lunar month, not Gregorian November, and the idiomatic line drops 皇子.

proposals.before: That August Wu besieged Jiangxia and struck Xiangyang; Grand Marshal Xuandi (Sima Yi) rescued Xiangyang and slew Wu generals such as Zhang Ba, matching the omens of war, mourning, and shifting sovereignty.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Wu besieged Jiangxia and struck Xiangyang; General-in-Chief Xuandi (Sima Yi) rescued Xiangyang and slew Wu generals such as Zhang Ba, matching the omens of war, mourning, and shifting sovereignty.
proposals.reason: 八月 is a lunar month, not August; 大將軍 is General-in-Chief, not Grand Marshal.

proposals.before: In the seventh month General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and fell to Shu’s army.
proposals.after: In the seventh month General of Chariots and Cavalry Zhang He pursued Zhuge Liang and was killed by Liang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 為亮所害 names Liang as the killer; fell to Shu’s army invents wording not in the sentence.

proposals.before: That December Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Grand Commandant Hua Xin died.
proposals.reason: 十二月 is a lunar month, not Gregorian December.

proposals.before: On wuwu in the tenth month the moon crossed the Winnowing Basket.
proposals.after: On jiawu in the tenth month the moon crossed the Winnowing Basket.
proposals.reason: Chinese 甲午 is the sexagenary day jiawu, not wuwu (戊午).

proposals.before: That tenth month, on wuwu, the Moon transgressed the Winnowing Basket.
proposals.after: That tenth month, on jiawu, the Moon transgressed the Winnowing Basket.
proposals.reason: Chinese 甲午 is jiawu; both English fields mistranslate it as wuwu.

proposals.before: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 the moon clipped the easternmost star of the Hairy Head.
proposals.after: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 of the Young Emperor the moon clipped the easternmost star of the Hairy Head.
proposals.reason: Chinese dates the omen under 少帝, which the idiomatic English omits.

proposals.before: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 the Moon transgressed the first star at the eastern end of the Hairy Head [Pleiades region].
proposals.after: On wuwu in the fourth month of Zhengshi 1 of the Young Emperor the Moon transgressed the first star at the eastern end of the Hairy Head [Pleiades region].
proposals.reason: Chinese 少帝 is missing from the literal English date formula.

proposals.before: In the third year’s third month Wang Ling and Prince Biao of Chu were exposed and killed for plotting, humbling the throne.
proposals.after: In the third year’s seventh month Wang Ling and Prince Biao of Chu were exposed and killed for plotting, humbling the throne.
proposals.reason: Chinese 三年七月 is the seventh month, not the third.

proposals.before: In the third month of the third year Wang Ling conspired with Prince Biao of Chu; both were executed; the ruler’s prestige thereafter sank.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of the third year Wang Ling conspired with Prince Biao of Chu; both were executed; the ruler’s prestige thereafter sank.
proposals.reason: Chinese 七月 is the seventh month; the literal English says third month.

proposals.before: During Wu’s Chiwu 13, fifth summer month, at the summer solstice Mars retrograded into the Southern Dipper.
proposals.after: During Wu, in Sun Quan’s Chiwu 13, fifth summer month, at the summer solstice Mars retrograded into the Southern Dipper.
proposals.reason: Chinese 吳孫權 names Sun Quan as the Wu ruler of the Chiwu year; the idiomatic English drops him.

proposals.before: At that time Wang Ling plotted to enthrone Prince Biao of Chu, saying “There is a star in the Dipper—someone base will suddenly rise to honor,” and questioned the star-clerk Haoxiang about it.
proposals.after: At that time Wang Ling plotted to enthrone Prince Biao of Chu, saying “There is a star in the Dipper—someone will suddenly rise to honor,” and questioned the star-clerk Hao Xiang about it.
proposals.reason: 暴貴者 means a person who suddenly becomes noble; 暴 is not “base,” and 浩詳 should not be fused as Haoxiang.

proposals.before: Empress Dowager Zhen died in the seventh month.
proposals.after: Empress Zhen died in the seventh month.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is 皇后甄氏, an empress, not an empress dowager.

proposals.before: In the second month Li Feng, his younger brother Li Yi, his father-in-law Zhang Ji, and others plotted sedition; the affair leaked and all were executed; Empress Zhang was deposed.
proposals.after: In the second month Li Feng, his younger brother Yi, the empress’s father Zhang Ji, and others plotted sedition; the affair leaked and all were executed; Empress Zhang was deposed.
proposals.reason: 後父張緝 identifies Zhang Ji as the empress’s father, not as Li Feng’s father-in-law.

proposals.before: Jingyuan 1’s fifth month brought the Chen Ji incident and Zhuge Dan’s destruction, matching the signs.
proposals.after: Jingyuan 1’s fifth month brought the Cheng Ji incident and Zhuge Dan’s destruction, matching the signs.
proposals.reason: Chinese 成濟 is Cheng Ji, not the surname Chen; the idiomatic rendering invents Chen Ji.

proposals.before: In the fifth month of Jingyuan 1 the Chen Ji coup and Zhuge Dan’s execution fulfilled it.
proposals.after: In the fifth month of Jingyuan 1 the Cheng Ji coup and Zhuge Dan’s execution fulfilled it.
proposals.reason: Chinese 成濟 is Cheng Ji; Chen Ji is a wrong romanization of 成.

proposals.before: In the second month of Jingyuan 1 of Emperor Yuan of Jin the Moon transgressed the Establishment Stars.
proposals.after: In the second month of Jingyuan 1 of Emperor Yuan the Moon transgressed the Establishment Stars.
proposals.reason: The heading is 元帝景元元年, the Cao-Wei Jingyuan reign of Emperor Yuan (Cao Huan). The literal line invents ‘of Jin’.

proposals.before: That November the armies advanced while Venus made its first evening appearance in the west.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month of the fifth year the armies advanced while Venus made its first evening appearance in the west.
proposals.reason: 五年十一月 is a lunar eleventh month of Xianning 5, not the Gregorian month November, and the year is omitted.

proposals.before: The emperor died on yiyou in Tixi 1’s fourth month.
proposals.after: The emperor died on yiyou in Taixi 1’s fourth month.
proposals.reason: 太熙 is Taixi, not Tixi.

proposals.before: On yiwei in the ninth year’s sixth month Venus appeared by daylight.
proposals.after: On yiwei in the sixth year’s tenth month Venus appeared by daylight.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六年十月乙未 is year 6, tenth month, day yiwei, not the ninth year’s sixth month.

proposals.before: On yiwei in the sixth month of the ninth year the Great White was seen in daytime.
proposals.after: On yiwei in the tenth month of the sixth year the Great White was seen in daytime.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六年十月 is the tenth month of the sixth year, not the sixth month of the ninth year.

proposals.before: After securing Luoyang Prince Qi remained as regent and slid into heedless arrogance.
proposals.after: After Prince Qi Jiong secured the capital, he remained to assist the government and then slid into heedless arrogance.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English fuses the capital with the prince as “Luoyang Prince Qi”; the Chinese is 齊王冏定京都.

proposals.before: Third year’s first month Sima Yue arrested Prince Changsha; Zhang Fang killed him.
proposals.after: In the first month of the third year Prince Donghai Yue seized Prince Changsha Yi, and Zhang Fang killed him.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 東海王越 rather than the unsourced surname Sima.

proposals.before: July saw Chen Zhen march the emperor west against Chengdu; the imperial hosts collapsed and threatened the sovereign’s train.
proposals.after: In the seventh month Chen Zhen led troops escorting the emperor against Chengdu; the six armies were routed and soldiers pressed the imperial carriage.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 奉帝伐成都 does not say the march was westward.

proposals.before: That year Gou Xi broke Gongshi Fan, Zhang Fang routed Prince Fanyang, western columns trapped Prince Hejian until he fled and Sima Yue killed him.
proposals.after: That year Gou Xi defeated Gongshi Fan, Zhang Fang crushed Prince Fanyang Xiao, western generals attacked Prince Hejian Yong—Yong fled, and Prince Donghai received and executed him.
proposals.reason: 迎殺之 is receive-and-kill by 東海王, not an unsourced surname Sima.

proposals.before: Guangxi 1’s fourth month showed Venus erratic, sliding from Wings down to Tail.
proposals.after: Guangxi 1’s fourth month showed Venus erratic, sliding from Wings into Tail and Winnowing Basket.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 箕 (Winnowing Basket), which the Chinese and the literal line include.

proposals.before: May brought Ji Sang’s assault on Ye—Feng Song met disaster, Sima Teng died, ten thousand fell, and Wei’s old palaces burned bare.
proposals.after: In the fifth month Ji Sang attacked Ye; Administrator Feng Song of Wei Commandery gave battle and was utterly defeated; Sang then slew Prince Teng of Eastern Yan, killed more than ten thousand, and burned the Wei-era palaces to ash.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops Feng Song’s office and battle and replaces the source title 東燕王騰 with an unstated personal name.

proposals.before: Then Sima Rui of Langye secured the southeast.
proposals.after: At that time the General Who Maintains the East, the Prince of Langye, first held Yangzhou territory.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names only 安東將軍、琅邪王 and 揚土; the idiomatic line invents the personal name Sima Rui and substitutes a vague southeast.

proposals.before: Yongchang 1’s third month Wang Dun struck Jiankang with river armies; imperial troops collapsed leaving only contrition.
proposals.after: Yongchang 1’s third month Wang Dun struck the capital with the hosts of Jiang and Jing; imperial troops collapsed leaving only contrition.
proposals.reason: 江荊之眾 are Jiang and Jing forces, not generic river armies, and the Chinese says 京都 rather than Jiankang.

proposals.before: In the third month of Yongchang 1 Wang Dun led Yang and Jiang armies against the capital; the six armies resisted but were routed, and the sovereign could only apologize.
proposals.after: In the third month of Yongchang 1 Wang Dun led the hosts of Jiang and Jing against the capital; the six armies resisted but were routed, and the sovereign could only apologize.
proposals.reason: Literal English misreads 江荊 as Yang and Jiang rather than Jiang and Jing.

proposals.before: April added Prince Cheng of Qiao and Gan Zhuo to the slaughter.
proposals.after: In the fourth month they also killed Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Sima Cheng of Qiao and General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits the offices 湘州刺史 and 鎮南將軍 and the surname 司馬.

proposals.before: Emperor Cheng’s Xianhe 6 first month bingchen placed the moon in the Dipper.
proposals.after: In Emperor Cheng’s Xianhe 6, on bingchen of the first month, the moon entered the Southern Dipper.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 月入南斗 states that the moon entered the Southern Dipper; the idiomatic English wrongly makes Emperor Cheng or the date ‘place’ the moon.

proposals.before: November stationed Mars on Stomach and the Hairy Head.
proposals.after: In that eleventh month Mars guarded Stomach and the Hairy Head.
proposals.reason: Chinese 熒惑守胃昴 is an astronomical stationing of Spark-Delight; ‘November stationed Mars’ treats the month as agent.

proposals.before: Eighth year’s eighth month ended Shi Le; Shi Hu usurped authority.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of the eighth year Shi Le died; Shi Hu seized power.
proposals.reason: Chinese 八年七月 is the seventh, not eighth, lunar month; 死 is death, not a vague ‘ended’.

proposals.before: In the eighth month of the eighth year Shi Le died and Shi Jilong seized power.
proposals.after: In the seventh month of the eighth year Shi Le died and Shi Jilong seized power.
proposals.reason: Chinese 七月 is the seventh month; the literal English invents an eighth month.

proposals.before: Fourth year second month Hu marched from Longxi, slew Duan Liao at Ji, failed against Murong Huang at Jicheng, lost Ma Qiu, and watched Huang execute Duan Liao.
proposals.after: In the second month of the fourth year he marched from Longxi, attacked Duan Liao at Ji, then struck Murong Huang at Jicheng without success; Huang routed his general Ma Qiu and captured Duan Liao, executing him.
proposals.reason: 攻殺於薊 is the attack at Ji, but the same sentence then has 虜段遼殺之, so ‘slew Duan Liao at Ji’ contradicts the later capture-and-execution by Huang.

proposals.before: the second year of Jianyuan saw Yu Bing’s death.
proposals.after: The second year of Jianyuan saw Yu Bing’s death.
proposals.reason: The English fragment begins in lowercase although it is presented as a complete sentence.

proposals.before: Yu Yi massed troops against Shi Hu, controlling the middle Yangzi and intimidating Jiankang.
proposals.after: Yu Yi massed great armies, planning to campaign against Shi Jilong, monopolizing the upper Yangzi while the court feared him.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has 專制上流 and 朝廷憚之; it does not name Jiankang or the middle Yangzi.

proposals.before: That year Shi Hu murdered Shi Sui, raided Didao, stacked troops east of Ji, and eyed Murong Huang.
proposals.after: That year Shi Jilong killed his son Sui, sent generals to raid and take Didao, camped east of Ji, and plotted against Murong Huang.
proposals.reason: The English omits 遣將, softens 謀 to “eyed,” and uses Shi Hu where the Chinese names 石季龍.

proposals.before: The following year Huan Wen invaded Shu, captured Li Shi, and shipped him east.
proposals.after: The next year Huan Wen likewise led a host to attack Shu, seized Li Shi, and sent him to the capital.
proposals.reason: 又輒率眾伐蜀 and 送至京都 name a host and the capital, not a shipment east.

proposals.before: Year five buried Chu Pou, general who conquered the north.
proposals.after: In the fifth year General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou died.
proposals.reason: 卒 means died, not buried.

proposals.before: Jiayin repeated the moon on Room.
proposals.after: On jiayin the moon transgressed Room.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 甲寅，月犯房 records a lunar transgression of Room; the idiomatic English invents “repeated the moon” and drops the moon as subject.

proposals.before: Tenth month jiaxu crossed the Neck.
proposals.after: In the tenth month, on jiaxu, the moon transgressed the Neck.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 月犯亢 has the moon as subject; the idiomatic line makes the day-name itself “cross” the asterism.

proposals.before: December buried Chu Pou.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Chu Pou died.
proposals.reason: 薨 means death of a high-ranking person, not burial; the literal rendering already has died.

proposals.before: Year seven Liu Xian slew Shi Zhi and generals, Shanxi erupted in turmoil and plague.
proposals.after: In the seventh year Liu Xian slew Shi Zhi and the various commanders; east of the mountains fell into turmoil, with pestilence and death.
proposals.reason: 山東 means east of the mountains, not the later province name Shanxi.

proposals.before: Loyal ministers suffer execution.
proposals.after: The prognostication said, "Loyal ministers will die by execution."
proposals.reason: The Chinese is an omen quotation introduced by 占曰; the idiomatic line drops that frame.

proposals.before: April’s campaign crushed Fu Jian’s Yaoliu corps.
proposals.after: In the fourth month Wen campaigned against Fu Jian and crushed his Yaoliu army.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Huan Wen (溫) as the commander and 苻健 (Fu Jian), which the idiomatic sentence omits as subject and merges into a possessive army label.

proposals.before: Twelfth year’s twelfth month saw Qi fall, Duan Kan captured, and three thousand slain.
proposals.after: Twelfth year’s eleventh month saw Qi fall, Duan Kan captured, and three thousand slain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 十一月 is the eleventh month, not the twelfth.

proposals.before: In the twelfth month of the twelfth year Qi city fell; Duan Kan was seized and more than three thousand were killed.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year Qi city fell; Duan Kan was seized and more than three thousand were killed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 十一月 is the eleventh month, not the twelfth.

proposals.before: Yonghe 3 brought Xianbei strikes on Hebei.
proposals.after: Yonghe 3 brought Xianbei strikes on the Yellow River and Ji.
proposals.reason: 河、冀 names the Yellow River and Ji Province, not the later regional label Hebei.

proposals.before: Prince of Kuaiji asked thrice to lower his rank three steps after Xi Tan and Xie Wan’s losses.
proposals.after: The Minister of Education, Prince of Kuaiji, citing the defeats of Xi Tan and Xie Wan, asked to take blame for the defeat and to demote himself three grades.
proposals.reason: 求自敗，求自貶三等 is a request to accept blame and a three-grade self-demotion, not a thrice-repeated plea; the idiomatic also drops 司徒.

proposals.before: Fourth month yihai crossed the Herdsman’s central star.
proposals.after: Fourth year’s first-month yihai crossed the Herdsman’s central star.
proposals.reason: Chinese 四年正月 is the first month of the fourth year, not the fourth month.

proposals.before: On jiwei the Great White entered the right-side gate of the Purple Forbidden Palace and exited through the Portal Gate.
proposals.after: On jiwei the Great White entered the right-side gate of the Supreme Palace and exited through the Portal Gate.
proposals.reason: Taiwei names the Supreme Palace enclosure, not the Purple Forbidden Palace; the idiomatic English already has Supreme Palace.

proposals.before: Fifth year’s first month buried Xi Tan.
proposals.after: Fifth year’s first month Xi Tan died.
proposals.reason: The source verb records death, not burial; the literal already says died.

proposals.before: Emperor Xiaowu’s Ningkang 1 New Year wushen occulted Antares.
proposals.after: On wushen in the first month of Emperor Xiaowu’s Ningkang 1, the Moon occulted Antares.
proposals.reason: Chinese 正月 is the first lunar month, not New Year, and 月 is the Moon as subject of the occultation.

proposals.before: July buried Huan Wen.
proposals.after: In the seventh month Huan Wen died.
proposals.reason: 薨 means died, not burial, and 七月 is the seventh lunar month rather than July.

proposals.before: Taixuan 1 Fu Jian took Liangzhou.
proposals.after: In Taiyuan 1 Fu Jian took Liangzhou.
proposals.reason: 太元 is the Taiyuan era, not Taixuan.

proposals.before: In Taixuan 1 Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou.
proposals.after: In Taiyuan 1 Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou.
proposals.reason: 太元 is the Taiyuan era, not Taixuan.

proposals.before: Taixuan 1 fourth month bingxu Mars crossed the Dipper’s third star.
proposals.after: On bingxu in the fourth month of Taiyuan 1, Mars crossed the Dipper’s third star.
proposals.reason: 太元 is the Taiyuan era, not Taixuan.

proposals.before: On bingxu in the fourth month of Taixuan 1 Spark-Delight transgressed the third star of the Southern Dipper.
proposals.after: On bingxu in the fourth month of Taiyuan 1 Spark-Delight transgressed the third star of the Southern Dipper.
proposals.reason: 太元 is the Taiyuan era, not Taixuan.

proposals.before: Seventh year fifth month bingzi Mercury crossed Regulus.
proposals.after: On bingzi in the seventh month of the fifth year, Mercury crossed Regulus.
proposals.reason: Chinese 五年七月 is the seventh month of the fifth year, not the fifth month of the seventh year.

proposals.before: On bingzi in the fifth month of the seventh year the Dawn Star transgressed the Chariot Shaft.
proposals.after: On bingzi in the seventh month of the fifth year the Dawn Star transgressed the Chariot Shaft.
proposals.reason: Chinese 五年七月 is the seventh month of the fifth year; the English fields reverse year and month.

proposals.before: Ninth year ninth month buried Empress Dowager Chu.
proposals.after: In the sixth month of the ninth year Empress Dowager Chu died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 九年六月 records death (崩) in the sixth month, not burial in the ninth month.

proposals.before: In the ninth month of the ninth year Empress Dowager Chu died.
proposals.after: In the sixth month of the ninth year Empress Dowager Chu died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 六月 is the sixth month, not the ninth.

proposals.before: Ninth month bingxu daylight Venus.
proposals.after: On bingxu in the seventh month of the ninth year, Venus was seen by day.
proposals.reason: Chinese 九年七月丙戌 is day bingxu of the seventh month of the ninth year.

proposals.before: On bingxu in the ninth month’s seventh day the Great White was seen in daytime.
proposals.after: On bingxu in the seventh month of the ninth year the Great White was seen in daytime.
proposals.reason: 丙戌 is a sexagenary day in the seventh month, not the seventh day of the ninth month.

proposals.before: Twelfth year saw Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Lü Guang carve independent realms.
proposals.after: In the twelfth year Murong Chui raided Dong’e, Zhai Liao struck the Yellow River, Yao Chang assumed a title at Anding, Fu Deng set himself up on Longshang, and Lü Guang seized Liang territory.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line collapses five distinct actions into a general claim that they carved independent realms, omitting the named places.

proposals.before: Those warlords then contested without pause.
proposals.after: Afterward Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong barricaded troops and vied for supremacy.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops the five named warlords that the Chinese and literal English both list.

proposals.before: Fourteenth year New Year bandits at Huangqiu fell to Liu Laozhi.
proposals.after: In the first month of the fourteenth year the Pengcheng spirit-bandits again assumed titles at Huangqiu, and Liu Laozhi destroyed them.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits Pengcheng origin, the spirit-bandit designation, and the assumption of titles.

proposals.before: September bingyin daylight Venus in Wings.
proposals.after: On bingyin in the ninth month daylight Venus in Zhen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 軫 is the Zhen lodge, not Wings (翼), which is the previous sentence’s asterism.

proposals.before: On bingyin in the ninth month it again appeared by day in the Wings.
proposals.after: On bingyin in the ninth month it again appeared by day in Zhen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 軫 is Zhen, not the Wings lodge 翼.

proposals.before: September repeated Venus in Wings.
proposals.after: In the ninth month it again appeared in Zhen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 軫 is Zhen, not Wings (翼).

proposals.before: In the ninth month it again appeared in the Wings.
proposals.after: In the ninth month it again appeared in Zhen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 軫 is Zhen, not the Wings lodge 翼.

proposals.before: Winter buried Yao Chang; his heir Yao Xing ascended the throne.
proposals.after: That winter Yao Chang died; his son Zilüe succeeded.
proposals.reason: Chinese 死 is death, not burial; 子略 is the successor’s courtesy name, not the given name 興 already used in the previous sentence.

proposals.before: That winter Yao Chang died; his son Yao Xing succeeded.
proposals.after: That winter Yao Chang died; his son Zilüe succeeded.
proposals.reason: Literal English substitutes given name Yao Xing for 子略 (Zilüe).

proposals.before: Tuoba Gui enthroned Wei at Zhongshan.
proposals.after: Prince of Wei Gui assumed the throne at Zhongshan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 魏王圭即位 is Gui, Prince of Wei, acceding, not ‘enthroning Wei’ as an object.

proposals.before: Xi Hui’s Huatai expedition against Murong Bao failed.
proposals.after: That June Xi Hui sent Zheng Qifang and others with ten thousand troops against Murong Bao at Huatai, and they returned defeated.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops named commander 鄭啟方, the force size, and the place name present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Huan Xuan broke Jingzhou; Yin Zhongkan died in Yongzhou.
proposals.after: Huan Xuan seized Jingzhou, and Yongzhou killed Yin Zhongkan and others.
proposals.reason: 雍州殺殷仲堪 makes Yongzhou the agent of killing, not merely the place of death; 等 is omitted.

proposals.before: July buried Grand Empress Dowager Li.
proposals.after: That seventh month Grand Empress Dowager Li died.
proposals.reason: 崩 is death of an empress dowager, not burial.

proposals.before: Sun En’s detachments failed against Liu Yu.
proposals.after: En sent another general to attack Guangling, killing more than three thousand, then withdrew to Yu Isle, at which time Liu Yu again pursued and defeated him.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence invents a failed Guangling attack and omits the slaughter, withdrawal, and named places.

proposals.before: October Yuanxian readied fleets against Huan Xuan.
proposals.after: In the tenth month Sima Yuanxian built a large river fleet intending to attack Xuan.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the surname 司馬 and the explicit purpose 將以伐玄.

proposals.before: March Huan Xuan seized Jiankang and killed Yuanxian.
proposals.after: In the third month Huan Xuan took the capital, killed Sima Yuanxian, and banished Grand Tutor Prince of Kuaiji Daozi.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 放太傅會稽王道子 and shortens 司馬元顯.

proposals.before: August bingyin occulted Venus on Right Enforcer.
proposals.after: On bingyin in the eighth month Venus occulted the Right Enforcer.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has 太白奄右執法: Venus is the subject that occults the Right Enforcer, not an occultation of Venus.

proposals.before: June jiachen occulted fourth Dipper star.
proposals.after: On jiachen in the sixth month the Moon occulted the Dipper’s fourth star.
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject is 月; the idiomatic English drops the Moon.

proposals.before: Huan Xuan seized the throne and exiled the imperial couple.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month of the second year Huan Xuan usurped the throne, banished the emperor and empress to Xunyang, and made Yong'an Empress He the Lady of Lingling.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence omits the date, Xunyang, and the reduction of Yong'an Empress He to Lady of Lingling.

proposals.before: Liu Yu wiped out the Huans.
proposals.after: In the second month of the third year Liu Yu wiped out the Huan clan.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits 三年二月.

proposals.before: In the third month’s second year Liu Yu extirpated the Huan clan.
proposals.after: In the second month of the third year Liu Yu extirpated the Huan clan.
proposals.reason: 三年二月 is the second month of the third year, not the third month of the second year.

proposals.before: The third year’s New Year wuxu brought retrograde Mars across the western Upper First Minister.
proposals.after: On wuxu in the first month of the third year retrograde Mars crossed the western Upper First Minister.
proposals.reason: 正月戊戌 is a day in the first month, not necessarily New Year’s Day.

proposals.before: April jiawu occulted Regulus’ second.
proposals.after: On jiawu in the fourth month the Moon occulted the second star of Xuanyuan.
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject is 月; the idiomatic English drops the Moon and compresses 軒轅第二星.

proposals.before: July buried Empress Dowager He.
proposals.after: In the seventh month Yong'an Empress He died.
proposals.reason: 崩 means she died, not that she was buried, and the date is the seventh lunar month of Yuanxing 3.

proposals.before: Yixi 1 March renchen occulted the Left Enforcer.
proposals.after: On renchen in the third month of Yixi 1 the Moon occulted the Left Enforcer.
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject is 月 (the Moon); the idiomatic English omits it and leaves an ungrammatical occultation clause.

proposals.before: November Wei Yongzhi died in Jingzhou.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month Inspector of Jingzhou Wei Yongzhi died.
proposals.reason: 荊州刺史 names his office; the idiomatic English turns Jingzhou into the place of death and drops the inspectorship.

proposals.before: Year two February Yiyang fell to rebels.
proposals.after: In the second month of year two Sima Guofan and others captured Yiyang.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 司馬國璠 as the attacker; the idiomatic English erases him into anonymous rebels.

proposals.before: September Rongqi died to Yang Chengzu’s hand.
proposals.after: In the ninth month Inspector of Yizhou Sima Rongqi was murdered by his adjutant Yang Chengzu.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English truncates 司馬榮期, omits 益州刺史, and conceals that the killer was his 參軍.

proposals.before: Murong Chao harassed the Huai north.
proposals.after: Murong Chao raided Xu and Yan; in the first month of the third year he again struck northern Xuzhou as far as Xiapi.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English collapses named provinces, a dated second raid, and Xiapi into a vague Huai-north phrase.

proposals.before: Year five Murong Chao struck Huainan.
proposals.after: In the fifth year Murong Chao again raided north of the Huai.
proposals.reason: 淮北 is north of the Huai; Huainan reverses the geography.

proposals.before: Fourth year April Kong Anguo died.
proposals.after: In the third month of the fourth year, Left Deputy Director Kong Anguo died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 三月 is the third month, not April, and the office 左僕射 is omitted in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: In the fourth month of the fourth year Left Deputy Director Kong Anguo died.
proposals.after: In the third month of the fourth year Left Deputy Director Kong Anguo died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 三月 is the third month; the literal English incorrectly says fourth month.

proposals.before: July bandits took Zoushan until Xu Yin repulsed them.
proposals.after: In the seventh month Sima Shufan and others seized Zou Mountain until Lu Commandery prefect Xu Yin drove them off.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the named commander 司馬叔璠 and the office 魯郡太守, replacing them with generic bandits.

proposals.before: Yao Xing’s strike on Bobo collapsed.
proposals.after: Yao Lue’s strike on Helian Bobo collapsed.
proposals.reason: The Chinese personal name is 姚略, not 姚興; Bobo is 赫連勃勃.

proposals.before: Yao Xing dispatched troops against Helian Bobo and suffered crushing defeat.
proposals.after: Yao Lue dispatched troops against Helian Bobo and suffered crushing defeat.
proposals.reason: The Chinese writes 姚略, which the literal English renders as Yao Xing.

proposals.before: August buried Empress Wang.
proposals.after: In the eighth month Empress Wang died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 崩 means the empress died, not that she was buried.

proposals.before: Shu rose once more and fell.
proposals.after: Shu rebelled again and was exterminated.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 蜀又反，討滅之 states a second rebellion followed by suppression, which “rose once more and fell” leaves vague and omits the punitive campaign.

proposals.before: Eighth year July guihai occulted Room.
proposals.after: On guihai in the eighth year’s seventh month the Moon occulted the second northern star of Room.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops the Moon as subject and the specification 房北第二星, making the omen unintelligible.

proposals.before: September purges continued.
proposals.after: In the ninth month Liu Fan and Xie Hun were executed, and Liu Yi was destroyed.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence invents a continuation of purges and omits the three named persons 劉蕃、謝混、劉毅 required by the Chinese.

proposals.before: December Shu collapsed.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month Zhu Lingshi extinguished Shu.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits the named commander 朱齡石 who is the grammatical subject of 滅蜀.

proposals.before: Year eleven Linyi struck Jiazhou.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year Linyi raided Jiaozhou and was repulsed.
proposals.reason: 交州 is Jiaozhou, not Jiazhou, and 距敗之 records that the raid was driven back, which the idiomatic sentence omits.

proposals.before: The omen-text says: “The ruler will suffer.
proposals.after: The omen-text says: “The ruler of men will have anxiety.”
proposals.reason: Literal English truncates 人君憂 and leaves the quotation unclosed.

proposals.before: Yixi 12 July Liu Yu attacked Later Qin.
proposals.after: In Yixi 12, seventh month, Liu Yu attacked Yao Hong.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English replaces the named person Yao Hong with the polity Later Qin.

proposals.before: Barbarians took Chang’an; Jin armies retreated east.
proposals.after: The next year western barbarians raided Chang’an; Inspector Zhu Lingshi’s hosts were lost and the imperial armies abandoned the west and went east.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops named commander Zhu Lingshi and the Yongzhou inspectorate.

proposals.before: Wu and Wei’s campaigns answered the comet.
proposals.after: Sun Quan mobilized along the Jiang-Huai chokepoints and besieged Xincheng to support Liang, while the Son of Heaven campaigned east against Quan.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English erases Sun Quan, Zhuge Liang, and the Son of Heaven.

proposals.before: Year two February Yuan expedition.
proposals.after: In the first month of the second year, [the court] campaigned against Gongsun Yuan (Wenyi).
proposals.reason: 正月 is the first lunar month, not February, and 公孫文懿 is Gongsun Yuan’s name, not a bare ‘Yuan expedition’.

proposals.before: In the second month of the second year he campaigned against Gongsun Yuan.
proposals.after: In the first month of the second year he campaigned against Gongsun Yuan.
proposals.reason: 正月 is the first month, not the second.

proposals.before: Third year New Year Ming died.
proposals.after: In the first month of the third year, Emperor Ming died.
proposals.reason: 三年正月 is the first month of year three, not a New Year paraphrase that drops the title 明帝.

proposals.before: In the third month’s first year of year three Emperor Ming died.
proposals.after: In the first month of year three Emperor Ming died.
proposals.reason: 正月 is the first month; the English reverses month and year.

proposals.before: Third year New Year emperor died.
proposals.after: In the first month of the third year the emperor died.
proposals.reason: 三年正月 is the first month of year three, not ‘New Year’.

proposals.before: In the third month’s first year the emperor died.
proposals.after: In the first month of year three the emperor died.
proposals.reason: 正月 is the first month, not the third month’s first year.

proposals.before: Qinglong 6 August comet in Seven Stars.
proposals.after: Zhengshi 6 eighth month: comet in the Seven Stars.
proposals.reason: The running years are 正始 of Shaodi, not 青龍; 六年八月 continues Zhengshi, not Qinglong.

proposals.before: Zhengyuan 1 Li Feng conspiracy died.
proposals.after: In Zhengyuan 1, Li Feng, his brother Yi, and the empress’s father Zhang Ji plotted; they were executed and the empress was deposed.
proposals.reason: 後父張緝 is the empress’s father, not Li Feng’s father-in-law; the compressed English also drops the deposing of the empress.

proposals.before: Three years later in Wei’s second year of Ganlu Zhuge Dan rebelled again in Wu while Wu sent rescuers.
proposals.after: Three years later in Wei’s second year of Ganlu Zhuge Dan rebelled again in Huainan while Wu sent rescuers.
proposals.reason: Chinese 又反淮南 locates Zhuge Dan’s revolt in Huainan, not in Wu; Wu only sent relief troops.

proposals.before: Wei Jingyuan 3 comet in Horn.
proposals.after: Wei Jingyuan 3 comet in Neck.
proposals.reason: The Chinese lodge is 亢 (Neck), not 角 (Horn), which was used correctly in the preceding Ganlu comet notice.

proposals.before: On renyin in the third year of Emperor Yuan of Wei’s Jingyuan era eleventh month a comet appeared in Horn white five cun, turning north, fading after forty-five days.
proposals.after: On renyin in the third year of Emperor Yuan of Wei’s Jingyuan era eleventh month a comet appeared in Neck white five cun, turning north, fading after forty-five days.
proposals.reason: Chinese 見亢 is the Neck lodge, not Horn.

proposals.before: Another saying: “When a comet appears in Horn the Son of Heaven loses virtue.
proposals.after: Another saying: “When a comet appears in Neck the Son of Heaven loses virtue.
proposals.reason: The quoted omen concerns 亢 (Neck), matching the idiomatic rendering, not Horn.

proposals.before: August Emperor Wen (Cao Pi) died.
proposals.after: August Emperor Wen died.
proposals.reason: After Xianxi 2 the 文帝 who died is Jin Emperor Wen, not Cao Pi; the parenthetical identification is false.

proposals.before: March buried Empress Dowager Wang.
proposals.after: March Empress Dowager Wang died.
proposals.reason: Chinese 崩 means she died; burial is not stated.

proposals.before: November comet at execution cart.
proposals.after: November comet at Xuanyuan.
proposals.reason: 斩辕 names the Xuanyuan asterism, not an execution cart.

proposals.before: the first year of Jianyuan November Horn comet.
proposals.after: In Jianyuan 1 eleventh month a comet appeared in Neck.
proposals.reason: 亢 is the Neck mansion, not Horn; the English is also an ungrammatical fragment.

proposals.before: On the sixth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jianyuan a comet appeared in Horn seven feet white.
proposals.after: On the sixth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jianyuan a comet appeared in Neck, seven chi long and white.
proposals.reason: 亢 should be Neck, matching the following omen unit.

proposals.before: Yonghe 5 November Horn comet.
proposals.after: Yonghe 5 November Neck comet.
proposals.reason: The Chinese lodges the comet in 亢 (Neck), not 角 (Horn).

proposals.before: On yimao in Yonghe 5 eleventh month a comet appeared in Horn.
proposals.after: On yimao in Yonghe 5 eleventh month a comet appeared in Neck.
proposals.reason: 亢 is Neck, not Horn.

proposals.before: Year six January Horn comet.
proposals.after: Year six January Neck comet.
proposals.reason: Again 亢, not Horn.

proposals.before: Year five May floods.
proposals.after: In the fourth year, in the fifth month, there were great floods under Heaven.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is 四年五月, the fourth year’s fifth month; the idiomatic English wrongly says “Year five”.

proposals.before: Murong Ke took Luoyang.
proposals.after: In the third month Murong Ke seized Luoyang, and Shen Jin and others died in battle.
proposals.reason: The Chinese records 沈勁等戰死, which the idiomatic English omits.

proposals.before: On dingsi in Ningkang 2 New Year a broom star appeared at Maid and Emptiness crossing Base, Horn, Chariot, Wings, Zhang.
proposals.after: On dingsi in Ningkang 2 first month a broom star appeared at Maid and Emptiness, crossing Base, Neck, Horn, Chariot, Wings, and Zhang.
proposals.reason: The Chinese sequence is 氐、亢、角、軫、翼、張; the literal English drops 亢 (Neck).

proposals.before: Fu Jian took Former Liang.
proposals.after: In Taiyuan 1, in the seventh month, Fu Jian took Liangzhou and captured Zhang Tianxi.
proposals.reason: 太元 is Taiyuan, 涼州 is Liangzhou rather than the polity label “Former Liang,” and 虜張天錫 is omitted.

proposals.before: In Taixuan 1 seventh month Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou and captured Zhang Tianxi.
proposals.after: In Taiyuan 1 seventh month Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou and captured Zhang Tianxi.
proposals.reason: 太元 is Taiyuan; “Taixuan” is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Taixuan 11 Dipper guest star.
proposals.after: Taiyuan 11 Dipper guest star.
proposals.reason: 太元 is Taiyuan, not Taixuan.

proposals.before: In Taixuan 11 third month a guest star stood in Southern Dipper until June.
proposals.after: In Taiyuan 11 third month a guest star stood in Southern Dipper until the sixth month.
proposals.reason: 太元 is Taiyuan; “Taixuan” is a mistransliteration.

proposals.before: Long’an 4 comet through palace stars.
proposals.after: On jichou in the second month of Long’an 4 a comet passed through the palace stars.
proposals.reason: The Chinese date is 隆安四年二月己丑; the idiomatic line drops the second month.

proposals.before: Huan Xuan exiled court.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month of the second year Huan Xuan usurped, banished the emperor and empress to Xunyang, and made Yong’an Empress He Lady of Lingling.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits 尋陽 and the demotion 以永安何皇后為零陵君.

proposals.before: Meteor fell toward Xiangping.
proposals.after: On the night of bingyin in the eighth month, a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with a bristled tail, streamed northeast from Mount Shou and fell southeast of the city of Xiangping.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits the dated night, length, color, origin at Mount Shou, and the fall southeast of Xiangping that the Chinese reports.

proposals.before: On bingyin night in August a great meteor tens of zhang long white with maned tail flowed northeast from Mount Shou past Xiangping’s southeast.
proposals.after: On bingyin night in the eighth month a great meteor tens of zhang long, white with a maned tail, flowed northeast from Mount Shou and fell southeast of Xiangping city.
proposals.reason: 墜 marks a fall onto the southeast of Xiangping, not a path that merely passed that sector.

proposals.before: Yuan died at meteor site.
proposals.after: In the ninth month Wenyi broke out of the siege, fled to where the star had fallen, and was beheaded; the city was slaughtered and his multitude buried alive.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops the breakout, beheading, massacre, and live burial that the Chinese narrates.

proposals.before: In the second year Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led over two thousand households to defect.
proposals.after: In the second year Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led more than two thousand retainers (buqu) to defect.
proposals.reason: 部曲 are military retainers, not households.

proposals.before: The Dipper governs executions; issuing from the handle means those wielding central killing power lack righteousness.
proposals.after: The Northern Dipper governs holding and killing; emerging from the Dipper bowl, the one who holds and kills occupying the center, is the image of injustice.
proposals.reason: 斗魁 is the bowl of the Dipper, not the handle, and 不直之象 is injustice rather than a generic lack of righteousness.

proposals.before: Yuan and Le butchered Bing.
proposals.after: The next year Liu Yuanhai and Shi Le attacked and plundered Bingzhou, with much slaughter.
proposals.reason: Yuan is ambiguous after Gongsun Yuan, and the line omits Bingzhou and the next-year dating.

proposals.before: Yue’s reprisals ravaged plain.
proposals.after: Sima Yue, angry that the lands east of Wei commandery and south of Pingyuan had sided with Sang, used rewards to Zhen and then raided until the ground was scorched.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line garbles 魏郡以東平原以南 and drops Sang, Zhen, and the scorched-earth outcome.

proposals.before: Yuan Zhen stripped.
proposals.after: The next year, envoys demoted Yuan Zhen to commoner.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 明年, 遣使, and 為庶人, leaving only a clipped name-plus-verb that does not report the dated demotion.

proposals.before: Shouchun succession.
proposals.after: Huan Wen was at Shouchun; Zhen died of illness, his son Jin succeeded and sought aid from Fu Jian.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line is a two-word caption and omits Huan Wen, Zhen's death by illness, the son's succession, and the appeal to Fu Jian.

proposals.before: Northern warlords contested.
proposals.after: After this, Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong each held troops and contended for supremacy.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic caption erases the five named warlords required for person extraction and the force-blocking sense of 阻兵爭強.

proposals.before: Zhang Dao defeated.
proposals.after: In the third month Zhang Dao took Hexiang and Taishan; Xiang Qinzhi attacked and drove him off.
proposals.reason: “Zhang Dao defeated” reverses the first clause (張道破合鄉、太山) and omits Xiang Qinzhi’s counterattack.

proposals.before: In the first year of Guangxi, White rainbow five nights.
proposals.after: In Guangxi 1, on jiashen in the twelfth month, a white vapor like a rainbow hung from mid-heaven down north to earth and was seen at night for five days before vanishing.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits 十二月甲申, the zenith-to-earth path, and that the vapor lasted five nights then disappeared.

proposals.before: Yue arrested Yin.
proposals.after: In the third month of the fourth year, Sima Yue arrested Miao Yin and others.
proposals.reason: The caption shortens 司馬越 and 繆胤 and drops 等 and the Yongjia 4.3 date carried from the narrative.

decisions.reason: Chinese 犯 is transgression/approach, not occultation (掩/奄). The repair restores the technical verb.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏文帝黃初四年三月癸卯，月犯心大星。

decisions.reason: November is a Gregorian month; the source is the eleventh lunar month, and 皇子 is omitted in the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十一月，皇子東武陽王鑒薨。

decisions.reason: August misreads 八月, and 大將軍 is Grand General, not Grand Marshal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 八月，吳遂圍江夏，寇襄陽，大將軍宣帝救襄陽，斬吳將張霸等，兵喪更王之應也。

decisions.reason: 所害 names Liang as the killer; “fell to Shu’s army” invents an army and drops the named agent.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其七月，車騎將軍張郃追諸葛亮，為亮所害。

decisions.reason: December is Gregorian; the source is the twelfth lunar month.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十二月，太尉華歆薨。

decisions.reason: 甲午 is jiawu, not wuwu (戊午).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其年十月甲午，月犯箕。

decisions.reason: 甲午 is jiawu, not wuwu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其年十月甲午，月犯箕。

decisions.reason: The source names 少帝; the original omitted the Young Emperor.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 少帝正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。

decisions.reason: The source names 少帝; the original omitted the Young Emperor.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 少帝正始元年四月戊午，月犯昴東頭第一星。

decisions.reason: The source month is 七月, not the third month.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三年七月，王淩與楚王彪有謀，皆伏誅，人主遂卑。

decisions.reason: The source month is 七月, not the third month.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三年七月，王淩與楚王彪有謀，皆伏誅，人主遂卑。

decisions.reason: 孫權 is the named dispatcher; dropping him invents an anonymous Wu command.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吳孫權赤烏十三年夏五月，日北至，熒惑逆行，入南斗。

decisions.reason: 暴貴者 is sudden nobility, not “the base”; 浩詳 is Hao Xiang. The original inverted the omen gloss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是時，王淩謀立楚王彪，謂「斗中有星，當有暴貴者」，以問知星人浩詳。

decisions.reason: 皇后 is Empress, not Empress Dowager.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 七月，皇后甄氏崩。

decisions.reason: 后父 is the empress’s father, not her brother.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二月，李豐及弟翼、後父張緝等謀亂，事泄，悉誅，皇后張氏廢。

decisions.reason: 成濟 is Cheng Ji, not Chen Ji.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 景元元年五月，有成濟之變及諸葛誕誅，皆其應也。

decisions.reason: 成濟 is Cheng Ji, not Chen Ji.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 景元元年五月，有成濟之變及諸葛誕誅，皆其應也。

decisions.reason: The source does not say “of Jin”; adding Jin invents a dynastic label for this Wei-period notice.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元帝景元元年二月，月犯建星。

decisions.reason: November is Gregorian; the source is the eleventh month of year five.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 五年十一月，兵出，太白始夕見西方。

decisions.reason: 太熙 is Taixi, not Tixi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太熙元年四月乙酉，帝崩。

decisions.reason: The source is year one, third month, not third-year first month.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六年十月乙未，太白晝見。

decisions.reason: The source is year one, third month, not third-year first month.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六年十月乙未，太白晝見。

decisions.reason: 齊王 is Prince of Qi; 洛 is Luoyang. The original fused them into “Luoyang Prince Qi.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 初，齊王冏定京都，因留輔政，遂專慠無君。

decisions.reason: The source does not name Sima; the invented personal name is unsupported here.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三年正月，東海王越執長沙王乂，張方又殺之。

decisions.reason: 七月 is the seventh lunar month, not July, and 西 is not in the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 七月，左衛將軍陳眕率眾奉帝伐成都，六軍敗績，兵逼乘輿。

decisions.reason: The source names offices and persons without the surname Sima; restoring the named agents is required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是年，苟晞破公師籓，張方破范陽王猇，關西諸將攻河間王顒，顒奔走，東海王迎殺之。

decisions.reason: 箕 is omitted in the original; both Winnowing Basket and Well are named.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光熙元年四月，太白失行，自翼入尾、箕。

decisions.reason: The source is Prince of Dongyan Teng sending a general; “Sima Teng” invents a surname and drops the office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 五月，汲桑攻鄴，魏郡太守馮嵩出戰，大敗，桑遂害東燕王騰，殺萬餘人，焚燒魏時宮室皆盡。

decisions.reason: 琅邪王睿 is Prince of Langye Rui; Sima is not in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是時，安東將軍、琅邪王始有揚土。

decisions.reason: 江荊 is Jiang and Jing, not “river armies”; 京都 is the capital, not Jiankang by name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 永昌元年三月，王敦率江荊之眾來攻京都，六軍距戰，敗績，人主謝過而已。

decisions.reason: 江荊 is Jiang and Jing, not Yang and Jiang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 永昌元年三月，王敦率江荊之眾來攻京都，六軍距戰，敗績，人主謝過而已。

decisions.reason: 四月 is the fourth lunar month, not April; named offices are omitted in the original.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 四月，又殺湘州刺史譙王司馬承、鎮南將軍甘卓。

decisions.reason: The moon is the transgressor; making Jupiter the agent reverses the syntax of 月犯歲星.
